verdict.rationale: Unstructured documents that partitioning turns files into structured document elements and metadata in a contextualized JSON format. It also offers a by-title chunking strategy, which implies section-aware grouping. The evidence never explicitly describes heading detection, parent/child section hierarchy, or reading-order preservation, so the structure-preservation claim is only partly supported. Missing for 10: explicit docs on heading/title element types and section hierarchy metadata, reading-order guarantees for complex layouts, independent or hands-on corroboration of structure fidelity.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, parsed output preserves document hierarchy — headings, sections, reading order — so downstream LLMs see structure, not soup

citations.quote: Partitioning converts content from unstructured files and semi-structured data records into structured document elements and metadata in a predefined, consistent, expressive, and contextualized JSON format.
You can further control this behavior with by title, by page, and by similarity chunking strategies.
